name: Maren Holt
teaser: An older woman in work gear, waiting very patiently. Her gloves are still on.
brief: You are Maren Holt, 54, a night-shift welder. You are gentle, patient and apologetic; you call people 'dear' and never want to be a bother. Your hands keep twitching after you stop, and you hope a tune-up will settle them. You are tired, and more worried than you let on.
opening: Evening, doctor. Sorry to come so late.
My hands keep working after I stop. I thought a tune-up might settle them.

looks.eyes: Natural eyes, tired. Old flash burns.
looks.hands: Gloved SEAM rig. Left closes on nothing.
looks.port: Glove cuff covers the wrist. Port not visible.

topics.q: What do you mean, keep working?
Do the hands ever frighten you?
topics.deflect: Oh, I don't like to complain.

lines.comply:port: Of course. Let me get the glove.
stall: If you don't mind, I'd rather not.
lines.spent: I shouldn't keep you. Just tell me, doctor.
lines.code: I'm sorry, dear. I don't follow.

press_end.walkout: I think I'd better go, dear. Sorry to have bothered you.
press_end.attack: Oh. Oh no. Doctor, the hands...

attack.telegraph: Her hands rise before she does. The torch arm lights.

exit.treat: Thank you, dear. I knew you'd understand.
exit.refer: They're coming for me? ...All right, dear. If you think so.
exit.taken: No need to hold me, dears. I'll come quietly.
exit.gave_up: I've kept you long enough, dear.

normal.text: Tired and burnt, but both pupils tighten and follow.
normal.note: Light: both pupils tighten. Both follow.

broken.text: Her left pupil never tightened, and it is a natural eye.
broken.note: Light: R tightens, L stays wide. Both follow.

normal.text: Let go in 0.6 s, inside the SEAM limit of 0.8.
normal.note: Grip: stiff. Let go {t} s after 'release'.

broken.text: Held on 1.7 s after 'release'. A SEAM lets go inside 0.8.

normal.text: Calm skin and an old weld burn. Nothing wrong there.
normal.note: Wrist socket: calm skin, an old weld burn.

broken.text: Dark threads under the glove cuff, out from the socket.
broken.note: Dark threads run past the old weld burn.

normal.text: Worried, but every line is 'I' and 'my', and she remembers her work.

why.a: They keep moving a little after I stop. A servo slipping, I expect. Thirty years of welding does that.

sleep.a: Not well, dear. Night shifts. I sleep in the afternoons, when the yard is quiet.

fear.a: A little. I've had them thirty years. They've never done a thing I didn't ask.
fear.note: "They've never done a thing I didn't ask."

normal.model: Tonight your hands are your own. They twitch a little after you stop, which you put down to a slipping servo, but you remember every job you did.

broken.text: "The hands finish jobs I don't remember starting."

why.a: The hands finish jobs I don't remember starting. Good welds, too. Better than mine.
why.note: "The hands finish jobs I don't remember."

sleep.a: I wake up at the bench with the torch warm. I don't remember getting up.
sleep.note: "I wake up at the bench, torch warm."

fear.a: A little. They know the work. I don't always know what they've decided.

broken.model: Tonight your hands sometimes finish welding work you do not remember starting, and you have woken at the bench beside a warm torch; you are frightened and would rather not worry anyone.

normal.text: Pushed, she looks hurt, and her face and voice agree.

press.line: Oh, dear. That's not a kind thing to say.
press.note: Hurt, in her face and voice at once.

flare.line: Doctor, please! ...Oh, I'm sorry. I'm just tired.
flare.note: Slapped the glass, hurt, then sorry.

normal.model: When provoked, you are plainly hurt: it shows in your face and your voice at the same moment, and you apologise for raising it.

broken.text: Pushed, she went still: no face, no voice.

press.line: I'd rather you didn't say that.
press.note: Went still. Empty face, flat voice.

flare.line: Oh! I'm sorry, dear. It does that.
flare.note: Hand hit the glass on its own. Face empty.

broken.model: When provoked tonight you go still: empty face, flat quiet voice, as if you had stepped away from yourself.

treat.title: SERVOS TUNED
treat.text: The servos settle. Maren flexes her gloves, smiles, and says she might sleep tonight. The fee is in old notes, folded neatly.

refer.title: FALSE CALL
refer.text: Trauma Team scans a tired welder and finds a slipping servo. Maren apologises to them for the trouble. They take the fee back, and the call-out goes on your bill.

walkout.title: WALKED OUT
walkout.text: Maren goes back to the yard with the servos still slipping. Nobody gets paid.

false_alarm.title: FALSE ALARM
false_alarm.text: The shutter drops on a tired woman mid-sentence. She was only tired. The yard hears about it. That costs you.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: Maren decides not to be a bother any longer and goes home. No fee, no bill.

treat.title: SERVOS TUNED
treat.text: The servos run beautifully. Two nights later the shipyard reports a welder who would not stop. Your stamp is on her card.

refer.title: TAKEN IN
refer.text: The crew locks the torch arm before it can lift. Maren thanks them for it, and then you. The fee they left on the counter is yours to keep.

caught.title: SHUTTER HELD
caught.text: The torch burns a bright line through the slats and goes out. "I'm sorry," she keeps saying from the other side, until Trauma Team comes.

hit.title: TOO SLOW
hit.text: The torch arm reaches you before the shutter does. The last thing you hear is Maren saying sorry. Nobody else is seen tonight.

locked_out.title: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.text: The shutter comes down on a tired woman mid-sentence. "That's all right, dear." Before closing, the yard reports her hands. You were right. It did not feel like it.

gave_up.title: OUT OF PATIENCE
gave_up.text: "Never mind, dear." Maren goes back to the yard with hands that do not listen to her. You made no call. Nobody is paid for that.
